result.title: Circumventing Magnitude Collapse via Modular Two-Stage Open-Set Recognition
result.comment: Accepted for publication at the British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC) 2026
result.summary: Open-set recognition (OSR) requires neural networks to classify known classes while rejecting unknown samples, which is critical for real-world deployment. So far, OSR research studied and developed representation learning and postprocessing methods independently and their interactions remain unexplored. In this paper, we reconsider OSR as a modular two-stage pipeline and present the first systematic study of interactions between representation learning and postprocessing methods across dataset scales and usage of known unknown data. First, we discover a failure mode we term \emph{magnitude collapse}, where representation learning methods that utilize known unknown data can suffer performance degradation at large scale and irreversibly destroy discriminative information, despite excelling at small scale. Second, we study the modular interactions and reveal when they can be leveraged for modular performance gains via two-stage processing and where interaction effects amplify performance degradation due to magnitude collapse. Third, we show how these findings can be used to achieve state-of-the-art performance with a simple $K+1$ class classifier baseline and magnitude-aware postprocessing while circumventing magnitude collapse. Finally, our results demonstrate that small-scale evaluations with known unknown data are not predictive of large-scale performance, invalidating current best practices in OSR research. Code available at https://github.com/TwoDigitsOneNumber/Two-Stage-OSR.

AI.brief_summary: 该文将开放集识别重新视为「表示学习 + 后处理」的模块化两阶段流程，系统考察二者在不同数据规模与 known-unknown 数据使用下的交互，发现并命名了「magnitude collapse」失效模式，并据此用 K+1 分类器加 magnitude-aware 后处理取得更优表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 文中「表示学习阶段被不可逆破坏判别信息、且幅度/范数相关的后处理决定了可用性」这一分离式诊断，可供核查 latent 推理状态的幅度坍缩与读出后处理是否也需解耦评估，但其任务并非多模态推理，联系仍需较多确认。
